correctness.rationale: For each determinant fibre, modal row A, modal column B and modal cell M give exact deletion counts s-A, s-B, s-M. Four elementary capacity inequalities yield the stated endpoints after summing fibres. For each admissible integer m, the explicit four-block fractional matrix satisfies every capacity and exact marked-row/column/cell constraint. The lower-bounded bipartite network has integer capacities, so integral feasible circulation produces a table with precisely those maxima. The b=1 or c=1 cases reduce to a one-dimensional distribution. The proof covers all sizes, all target alphabets, and all integer values in the interval. Independent small-instance enumeration and a separate integral-flow construction checked 339613 tables, 3373 constructions, and 9984 multi-fibre instances; finite checks are supplementary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generality of objects is not a domination test by itself: a fixed-margin enumeration algorithm does not prove a sharp closed threshold when only the largest margins are specified. The new statement is all-n, all-b,c, all-admissible-error and integer-interpolating. A hidden stronger theorem in this broader literature remains a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full-text approximation paper gives a deletion-distance definition, missing-rule example and unary completeness, but does not present a closed feasible triple spectrum at fixed n and two target alphabet bounds. Classical fixed-margin contingency-table enumeration solves a richer numerical data input problem but does not state the compressed max-row/max-column/max-cell feasible interval or sharp approximate-dependence inference rule. Relevant published comparisons involving splitting disjunctions, soft repairs and minimal falsifiers concern distinct operations or measures. Current searched evidence shows no dominating explicit statement; residual historical-priority risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Approximate joint functional dependence is a natural database/team-semantic error measure. The theorem determines the entire exact feasible integer region for two output alphabets of arbitrary sizes, all team sizes and determinants, including a sharp alphabet-sensitive logical implication that can strictly improve the ordinary additive deletion bound. The integer interpolation and circulation construction allow exact stress-case generation rather than numerical examples. The quantified family and sharp optimality make this a motivated structural classification, not an arbitrary isolated finite table.
